title: Kindness
human_question: What does a good mind feel like from the inside, and what does it make possible?
journey: Chathura meets people who give, care, forgive and trust: alms-givers, caregivers, teachers, strangers who help.
surface: Generosity, gratitude, compassion and quiet faith, and the ease that comes with them.
depth: Goodness is not one thing but a team: nineteen beautiful factors arise together in every good mind, including lightness, pliancy and ease, so kindness is also a kind of relief. Compassion, sympathetic joy and wisdom join when conditions allow. Good action has its own results. The four sublime abidings turn kindness into a practice.

arc.opening: Something given freely. Object 6 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Generosity, restraint, compassion, shared joy and faith, each through real people and real acts.
arc.closing: Caring for others leads to the body: the sick, the old, the tired.

concepts.role: The eight wholesome sense-sphere minds: everyday goodness, with or without wisdom, joyful or calm.
The eight resultant minds with roots: the fruit that good action brings back.
The fifty-two mental factors: the whole team that travels with each mind.
The nineteen beautiful universal factors: faith, mindfulness, conscience, restraint, non-greed, non-hatred, balance, and six pairs of ease and flexibility.
The six variable beautiful factors: three abstinences, compassion, sympathetic joy, wisdom.
The mental-factor make-up of each beautiful sense-sphere mind.
Recollection of the Buddha: faith as a practice.
The four sublime abidings: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Goodness is not one feeling but a whole team of qualities that arrive together, and among them are calm, lightness and softness, so being kind also takes weight off the one who is kind. It shows up in giving, in refusing to cheat, in gladness at others' luck, and in care that changes shape for each person who needs it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: යහපත් සිත එක් හැඟීමක් නොව එකට පහළ වන ගුණ කණ්ඩායමක් වන අතර, එහි සන්සුන් බව, සැහැල්ලු බව හා මෘදු බව ද ඇති බැවින් කරුණාව කරන්නාටත් සහනයක් වේ. දීමෙන්, වංචාවෙන් වැළකීමෙන්, අනුන්ගේ සතුටට සතුටු වීමෙන් සහ එක් එක් කෙනාගේ අවශ්‍යතාවට ගැළපෙන රැකවරණයෙන් එය පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that a mind never arises alone but together with its mental factors, and that in every good mind nineteen beautiful factors are present at once, among them faith, mindfulness, non-greed, non-hatred, balance, and paired qualities of tranquillity, lightness, softness, workability, proficiency and straightness. Everyday goodness, called 'great' because it is common to many, comes in eight kinds: joyful or even, with or without understanding, prompted or unprompted. Other beautiful factors join only when conditions call for them: an abstinence when a real wrong is refused, compassion when someone suffering is in view, sympathetic joy when someone happy is in view. The four sublime abidings, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and equanimity, turn these responses into a practice extended to all beings, and the texts teach that good action has results of its own, though not as a quick reward.
progression: EPD-0048 The Free Table: everyday giving is the 'great' goodness, common to many, and it counts whether done with joy or as a quiet habit.
EPD-0049 Fair Measure: goodness can be a refusal; right livelihood exists in the moment a real chance to cheat is turned down.
EPD-0050 A Good Catch Day: gladness at someone else's luck is its own quality, the opposite of envy, meant to reach anyone.
EPD-0051 The Softening: every good mind includes a softness against pride and fixed views, like a hide worked until it can be used.
EPD-0052 The Society Book: refusing to profit from a member's trouble is right livelihood made communal, and good action has results of its own.
EPD-0053 The Face Taking Shape: faith is practised through careful attention to good qualities, and the mind settles into joy and calm.
EPD-0054 Four Shapes of the Same Care: one care takes four shapes, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and equanimity, depending on what is needed.
EPD-0055 Setting the Load Down: lightness and tranquillity come with every good mind, so kindness is also a kind of relief.
EPD-0056 Between Two Rounds: compassion and gladness each answer the person actually in view, so a carer moves between them.
EPD-0057 The Tea Round: compassion and gladness take turns and never fill the same moment, and kindness begins to meet the body's fragility.
lesson.builds_on: The previous stage slowed perception down until a gap appeared inside each moment, the point of impulsion where choice is made and action begins; this stage shows what the mind is like, from the inside, when that choice goes toward goodness.
lesson.hands_to_next: Caring for others has led to bodies that tire, sicken and age, so the next stage asks what the body itself is made of and why decay is written into it.
